The depth map clearly distinguishes foreground depth layers—for example, the yellow-hoodie woman passing in front of the maroon-jacket and striped-shirt women—and the floor-to-column geometry that looks flattened in the wide-angle RGB. However, it lacks facial and gaze information: the RGB reveals the yellow-hoodie woman looking toward the camera wearer in frames 1–4 before turning away in frame 5, while the other women mostly orient inward toward the group. It also blurs depth boundaries around airborne hair and distant background pedestrians.
segmentation: Against a black backdrop, the segmentation view separates individual foreground and background people as well as several wall-mounted items. It displays five principal foreground `person` masks grouped about 0.5–3.5 m in front of the camera wearer, with roughly 0.5–1.5 m spacing, plus smaller background `person` masks around 4–7 m behind them near the ATM/kiosk on the left. A `handbag` detection accompanies them in frames 4–5, though the object is actually a white pack/bag carried at hip height. The map draws attention to distant, partly hidden pedestrians near the green ATM and to a small screen labeled `tv` high along the upper-left/upper-right edge, approximately 6–8 m away and above head level, all of which can be missed easily in the crowded RGB strip. Nevertheless, several outputs are unreliable: in frames 3–5, it wrongly labels the painted mural figure on the back wall—about 8–10 m away and upper-right of the central pillar—as a `person`; it breaks apart or loses masks for strongly occluded background people; and its 2D silhouettes cannot convey 3D distance or establish whether anyone is facing the camera wearer.
pose: On a black field, the pose visualization shows sparse yellow 2D body keypoints while leaving out the entire room arrangement, every background pedestrian, and four of the five foreground women positioned roughly 1–3.5 m from the camera wearer. Frame 1 captures only the upper torso and lifted arms of the woman in the patterned beige jacket. She stands centrally about 2.5–3 m away, facing roughly toward the camera wearer and the foreground group, with both hands raised to her head. In frames 2–5, the tracker changes targets and follows only the head/face plus one torso-to-hip line belonging to the grey-top woman on the right, who is around 1.2–1.8 m away. These minimal points record the grey-shirt woman's slight torso movements and left-facing head direction on the right side across frames 2–5 without adding visual clutter, but nearly all environmental and spatial context must be recovered from the RGB image. Overall, the pose map is very unreliable: despite visible hands lying within arm's reach of the subjects' own heads and torsos, it detects none of the magenta hand skeletons; it entirely misses both the approaching yellow-hoodie woman, about 0.5–1.5 m away and cropped at the lower edge, and the women on the left; and every frame contains malformed, incomplete stick segments.
